clue.text: Old hat-raising in the summer-house, for example

parts.note: something old hat is passé, out of fashion, so simply out
raising a structure is building it

explanation.surface: Someone finds an antique hat being lifted inside a garden summer-house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' reads as a hat that is old, but it is one idea: out of date, OUT. 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer-house is one example of a minor structure standing apart from the main house.

clue.text: Relative spotted with no article

indicators.note: with no tells us a piece is to be dropped from the longer word

parts.note: spotted in the sense of dirty or stained, so unclean
an is the indefinite article in grammar

explanation.surface: A family member is noticed without any piece of clothing on.
explanation.definitionFit: A father's or mother's brother is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Top gear for father?

parts.note: top gear reads as a car's highest ratio, but means headwear, and father is a Catholic priest

explanation.surface: Dad's car is shifting into its highest gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The British TV motoring show Top Gear and a car's top gear both lurk; the hat is the square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Priests addressed as Father wear this square cap with ridges on top, so it is clerical headwear.

clue.text: Yoke for 22,well inside hotel

indicators.note: inside says the spring word is placed within the lodging word

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
a spa is a mineral spring or well

explanation.surface: Gear for an expedition is placed carefully within a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: A South African term, to harness oxen to a wagon, apt for the safari at 22. The '22,well' spacing is an OCR join.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Africa the verb means to harness draught animals to a wagon, the job of yoking them before a trek.

clue.text: Don Brook creation that is turned by hand

indicators.note: creation says these letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A man called Don Brook has made something that gets rotated manually.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Brook looks like a person, but his name is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A round door handle is twisted by the hand to open the latch.

clue.text: Clear round called in this game for ladies

parts.note: net profit is what is clear after deductions
a ball is a round object, a sphere

explanation.surface: A clear round is announced in a sport played by women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called in' is a link. Netball, a court game close to basketball, is chiefly played by women in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport of passing a ball to shoot into a high ring is traditionally a women's team game.

clue.text: Assortment item, of interest to numismatists

definitions.meaning: a miscellany of odds and ends
... were both old names for coins, as in pieces of eight and threepenny bits

explanation.surface: A mixed lot contains one thing that coin collectors would like.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds and ends form a miscellany, while bits and pieces are also coins a collector of money would seek.

clue.text: Grant, for example, in cinerama production

indicators.note: production says the letters are made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Cary Grant appears in a widescreen cinema film production.
explanation.walkthrough: Grant could be the film star Cary Grant (born British, later a US citizen) or President Ulysses S. Grant; either way a citizen of the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses Grant was a US president, so he exemplifies a citizen of the United States.

clue.text: Awareness of lower position

definitions.meaning: comprehension or grasp of a situation
read as two words, a standing under something, beneath it

explanation.surface: Someone becomes conscious of their junior status.
explanation.definitionFit: Comprehension is awareness; split in two, the word describes standing beneath, a lower place.

clue.text: Suffer some plain curiosity

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone endures a measure of straightforward nosiness.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a loss or penalty on oneself is to suffer it.

clue.text: Blue, perhaps, but a good loser

definitions.meaning: a Blue is an athlete who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University
someone who takes defeat with grace and fair play

explanation.surface: An Oxbridge athlete is described as gracious in defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a Blue is awarded for competing against the rival university. The clue is singular, so the grid wants the man, not the men.
explanation.definitionFit: A Blue is an athlete, and one who loses gracefully shows fair play, both senses of the word.

clue.text: Flattery heard after dinner?

definitions.meaning: speech heard over the sweet course, dessert, at a dinner

explanation.surface: Compliments are offered in speeches following a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the sweet is the dessert course, so talk over it is sweet talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaxing, flattering words are a form of flattery; split, the phrase is conversation over dessert.

clue.text: A place for putting unfinished suit

indicators.note: unfinished says the word's last letter is cut off

parts.note: on a golf course, putting is done on the green

explanation.surface: A golfer's spot for putting hosts a business suit left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing but is the verb: to be suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense: food that does not suit you does not agree with you.

clue.text: Sauna's out of order-the place is sub-tropical!

indicators.note: out of order says these letters are not in their proper sequence

explanation.surface: A broken sauna seems odd when the weather is warm anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's gives an S here. Nassau is the capital of the Bahamas.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau, capital of the Bahamas, lies in a warm sub-tropical zone, the place meant.

clue.text: Service dress is too much, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a surplus is an amount that is too much, an excess

explanation.surface: Someone complains a formal outfit is excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' is a church service, not military.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose white vestment is worn by clergy and choir at a church service.

clue.text: Bank security devices used by oarsmen

parts.note: a bank of things is a row of them
locks keep doors and safes secure

explanation.surface: A bank installs security devices, which rowers also use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank security' suggests a vault, but splits as row and locks.
explanation.definitionFit: Oars pivot in these fittings on the gunwale, things a rower uses.

clue.text: Storm lantern used by those taking coats off?

definitions.text: used by those taking coats off?

parts.note: a blow is a gale or storm
a lantern is a kind of lamp

explanation.surface: A storm lantern is used by people removing their coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coats' are coats of paint, stripped with a flame torch.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's flame torch softens old paint so coats of it can be scraped off.

clue.text: Set for Spanish spread…

parts.note: por is Spanish for for
a spread of food is laid on a table

explanation.surface: A dining set suited to a Spanish feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is a TV or radio set, one that can be carried about.
explanation.definitionFit: A carryable television or radio receiver is a type of set, often simply called a portable.

clue.text: A step up?

parts.note: a stride is a long step

explanation.surface: A step upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' as a rider is up: in the saddle with a leg on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: A mounted rider sits with legs either side of the horse, said to be up.

clue.text: … the Spanish gooseberry?

parts.note: gooseberry is British slang for a third person spoiling a couple's privacy, here a Spanish chaperone

explanation.surface: A Spanish table is spread with gooseberries.
explanation.walkthrough: Continues 18 across's ellipsis. To play gooseberry, in Britain, is to be the unwanted third person with a courting couple.
explanation.definitionFit: An older woman acting as chaperone to girls in a Spanish family is the classic watching third party.

clue.text: Bring down someone of 19

parts.note: someone sitting with legs either side of a mount is knocked from the saddle

explanation.surface: Someone straddling is brought down.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a rider from the saddle is to bring down one seated on a horse.

clue.text: The expedition is mainly secure, air-conditioned

indicators.note: mainly says most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: secure means safe

indicators.note: conditioned says these letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: The trip is mostly safe and has air conditioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conditioned' turns AIR into ARI; 'mainly' cuts SAFE to SAF.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting or viewing trip into the African bush is an expedition.

clue.text: Showy effect of intricate lace type of shirt

indicators.note: intricate says the letters are twisted into a complicated new pattern

parts.note: a T-shirt is a type of shirt

explanation.surface: An elaborate lace detail adds flair to a style of shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant flair or a striking flourish is a showy effect.

clue.text: Affected by exposure, but came through

definitions.meaning: worn or discoloured by wind and rain

explanation.surface: Someone was battered by the elements but survived.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood left outdoors becomes worn by the elements; to survive a storm is to come through it.

clue.text: General survey announced for theatrical entertainment

indicators.note: announced signals that the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a review is a general survey of something

explanation.surface: An overview is publicised for a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A light stage show of sketches, songs and dances is a theatrical entertainment.

clue.text: Dish left in derelict hacienda

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
derelict says the word is ruined, its letters broken up

explanation.surface: A meal has been abandoned inside a ruined Spanish farmhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derelict' rearranges HACIENDA, and 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This rolled tortilla with a filling and chilli sauce is a Mexican dish.

clue.text: Glossy bird of prey

definitions.meaning: a large black crow with shiny plumage
as a verb, to hunt for prey or devour greedily

explanation.surface: A shiny bird is described as a predator.
explanation.definitionFit: The large black crow has glossy plumage; the old verb means to seek prey and plunder.

clue.text: Outfielder yawning-feeling off!

parts.note: a yawning chasm is deep

indicators.note: off says the letters are disordered, not right

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder yawns because they feel unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges FEELING into FINELEG. Deep fine leg is a cricket fielding position behind the batter on the leg side, near the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: This cricket position is far out on the leg side behind the batsman, so its occupant is an outfielder.
